transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's real nice to meet you too. Am I okay sitting right here? Okay, good. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, it's a little embarrassing, to be honest. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for it, it was really just a misunderstanding. I had a bit of a moment at work. I'm a personal care aide, and we had this staff meeting... and I just got a little overly enthusiastic, I suppose. 

I got pretty worked up and started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill for everybody. I was just trying to be helpful, you know? But I was using the chairs and waving my arms all around to demonstrate, and... well, the embarrassing part is, when folks told me to sit down, I just couldn't seem to stop. I didn't mean to cause a fuss or be disruptive, I promise. I just got a bit carried away. Does that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?

Oh, um... well. I wouldn't say I'm seeing things, or anything like that. I promise I have a good head on my shoulders. But... I guess, sometimes... well, I hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying this, but sometimes when it's real quiet? Like if I'm all alone in the hallway at the facility, or just at home by the laundry room, I'll hear my name. Or I'll hear one of the residents calling out for help, clear as day. 

But then I go to check on them, and... well, there isn't anybody there. I always just figure it's my ears playing tricks on me, you know? Because I'm so used to listening out for the folks at work, my brain just sort of fills it in. That's a pretty normal thing to happen, right? I really hope that doesn't sound too strange... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I've been feeling, you know, out of control or anything like that. I'm usually a pretty even-keeled guy. But I guess... lately, there are these stretches where I just feel really bright, you know? Like I'm all fired up and everything is finally lining up perfectly for me. It feels good, honestly. I get a lot done. 

But then... well, this is the part I feel a little bad about. If someone slows me down when I'm feeling like that, or if they question what I'm doing—like at the staff meeting—I guess I can get a little snappy. I end up snapping at folks harder than I mean to. I always apologize right after, because I really don't like being rude. It's just... I get so focused on helping, and it's frustrating when people don't see it the same way. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a difficult person to work with, because I really do try my best to get along with everyone.
When you’re in those bright, fired-up stretches, do you need less sleep than usual?

Well, um... I guess so, yeah. But I don't feel tired or worn out, I promise. It's actually kind of nice. I'll sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I'm just... awake. Right before dawn. 

I wake up feeling totally refreshed and ready to go. I don't think there's anything wrong with it, really. It gives me a chance to sit up while the house is still quiet and dark, and I can just make all my plans for the day without anyone bothering me. I get a head start on everything, you know? It's just me being productive. That's a good thing, right? I mean, a lot of successful folks don't need much sleep, isn't that what they say? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
When you hear your name or someone calling for help, does that happen only during those bright, fired-up periods?

Well, um... I wish I could say it was just when I was all fired up. That would make sense, right? But... well, I want to be completely honest with you so I'm doing this right. There was a stretch a little while back where things were real calm for me. I was sleeping my normal hours again, just taking it easy, not rushing around trying to finish a dozen extra projects at once. Just a regular, quiet few weeks. 

But, um... I still kept hearing my name in the hallways during that time. And... oh boy, I feel a little silly even bringing this part up, because I really don't want you to think I'm one of those paranoid types. But for those several weeks, I was also just so sure that the other staff at work were keeping notes on me. Like, secretly writing things down about my shifts behind my back. 

I mean, it's not too strange to think coworkers might gossip or keep tabs on you, right? That kind of stuff happens at every job, doesn't it? I just try to keep my head down and be a good employee. I hope telling you that doesn't make me sound bad... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture like I'm supposed to.
For at least 2 weeks, have you had those voices or beliefs about coworkers keeping notes on you during a time when you were not in one of those bright, fired-up periods?

Yeah, um... exactly. Like I was trying to say just a minute ago, I hope I explained it okay. There was definitely a stretch for, well, several weeks where things were real calm. I was sleeping my regular hours again and I wasn't rushing around trying to do a bunch of extra projects. 

But during those few weeks... I still heard my name being called out. And I still stayed convinced that people at work were keeping those notes on me. I really hate admitting that, because I know how it sounds, and I really want you to see that I'm a reasonable guy. But yes, it was for at least a couple of weeks while I wasn't feeling fired up at all. 

Is that... is that the kind of detail you needed? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for so we can get this right.
Have you ever been hospitalized because of one of these fired-up periods?

Oh, no, no. I've never had to go to the hospital for being too fired up. Um... I really try to keep things manageable, you know? Like I was saying, I mostly just use that extra energy to get things done around the house, I don't let it get out of hand. 

I work as a personal care aide, so I know hospitals and facilities are for folks who are really in a bad way, and I'd never want to cause a fuss or take up a bed when someone else needs it more. I promise I'm not that kind of trouble. I've always been able to just handle myself at home. That's a good sign, right? I mean, staying out of the hospital means I'm doing pretty okay, doesn't it?

During one of those fired-up periods, have your symptoms ever gotten so severe that they caused major problems in your life—like getting suspended or fired, getting into serious trouble, or not being able to function normally?

Well, um... I really wouldn't call them major problems. I mean, I'm still trying my best to keep things together, you know? But, um... I guess things did get a little complicated at work. They, uh... they put me on leave from the senior center for a bit. Just a temporary thing, I'm sure! I just... I worry a lot about whether I can safely go back to caregiving right now. I don't want to let anyone down.

And, well, at home... my wife has had to step in a bit more. She's been having to remind me about my chores and, um, my appointments. I haven't been keeping up quite the way I usually do, which I feel terrible about. I always want to be a good husband and pull my weight. I've also, um, kind of pulled back from my church friends lately. I just haven't been myself. 

I hope you don't think less of me for struggling with all this. I'm really trying hard to get back on track. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
During one of those fired-up periods, did you ever become so convinced of something unusual or hear voices more strongly than usual?

Well, um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, I don't want to make it sound worse than it was, because I was still getting a lot done, you know? But, um... when I was in one of those fired-up stretches, where I was only sleeping maybe a couple hours a night and making all those big plans for the house... I was also, well, I was still hearing my name being called out when no one was there. 

And, um, I also got really... well, I felt pretty sure my supervisor at the center was setting traps for me. Like, trying to catch me doing something wrong so they could fire me. I know that probably sounds a little crazy, and I really hope you don't think I'm a difficult employee or anything. I just... it felt so real at the time. I'm usually a very trusting person, I promise. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can figure this out.
